proxy_language: Classical Greek (Attic/Koine) with Rhodian (Doric) dialect features; used as the nearest attested proxy because 'Teinedeired' is not a recognised attested ethnonym or language
proxy_rationale: No attested culture or language called 'Teinedeired' is known to me. The region tag (Rodos = Rhodes) and kind (later court) point to Hellenistic/Rhodian Greek, a Doric-dialect Greek-speaking polity (c. 4th-1st c. BCE) with a maritime court and Colossus tradition. The current game strings (Rusukierkkurrak, Stiubamairteòilaskaig etc.) look Gaelic/Brittonic-flavoured and do not match Greek; they are not usable as evidence. Greek is therefore a defensible regional proxy, but the link to the named culture is weak and may be wrong if Teinedeired is a fictional or non-Greek court. Do not treat output as attested Teinedeired.
phonology: Classical/Hellenistic Greek, Doric colouring. Consonants: stops p t k, b d g (voiced; spirants in Koine), aspirates ph th kh (Classical; fricatives f th x in later Koine), s (z = /zd/ or /z/), m n, l r, h (rough breathing). Vowels: a e o i u plus long a: e: o:, and diphthongs ai ei oi ui au eu ou. Doric retains long a where Attic has long e (e.g. Dor. hamera vs Att. hemera; Dor. nasos vs Att. nesos). Rhodian is Doric of the 'mild' type (Dorian Hexapolis).
phonotactics: Syllables (C)(C)V(C) with V short or long/diphthong. Onsets may be single C or clusters of stop+liquid (pl kl tr gr), s+stop (sp st sk), stop+nasal (kn gn), s+stop+liquid (str spl skl). Word-final consonants are restricted to n r s (and x ps from k/p + s); no other final stops. Every word has an accent (acute/grave/circumflex), not marked in plain Latin transliteration. Hiatus is tolerated within words. Initial rh- and h- (rough breathing) occur.
orthography: Standard scholarly Latin transliteration: ph th kh for aspirates, ps ks, rh, y for upsilon (u in diphthongs), ch optional for chi, h for rough breathing, macrons optional for long vowels (e: o: or e o without marks). Use i/u in diphthongs (ai ei oi ui au eu ou). Accents omitted for game use. Doric forms may use a for Attic e (a-dialect: Hamera, Nasos, Damos).
morphology: Fusional, inflecting language. Nouns: 3 genders, 5 cases (nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, vocative), 3 numbers (sg, du, pl); declensions: 1st (a-stems), 2nd (o-stems), 3rd (consonant/i/u-stems). Verbs: thematic and athematic, augment, reduplication. Adjectives agree with nouns. Word forms are citation forms ending in -a/-e (f), -os/-on (2nd decl m/n), -is/-ys, -s, -n, -r, -ks, etc.
compounding: Compounds are very productive: first element (stem + linking vowel -o-, or -i-/-a-) + second element; head is the right-hand member, e.g. theo-doros 'gift of god'. Verbal compounds: first = object/modifier, second = agent noun in -os/-es, e.g. nauarkhos 'ship-ruler', politarkhes. Genitive constructions: Y-gen X (noun + genitive after), but the article lets genitive precede or follow; names are often X-gen or compounded. Suffixes: -ion (place/temple: Heraion), -eion (Mouseion), -ia (festival Halieia 'of Helios'), -eus agent, -ter/-tor agent, -ma/-sis action/result, -ia/-ike abstract.
noun_phrase_order: Adjective + noun or noun + adjective both occur with the article (ho agathos aner / aner ho agathos). In name-building use Adjective + Noun (head last) or Noun + Genitive. Genitive of possession follows head noun or sits between article and noun. Prepositions precede noun in dative/accusative/genitive.

notes: No attested language 'Teinedeired' is known to me; the proxy is Rhodian Doric Greek chosen on region and period, with low confidence. The given game names appear Celtic/Gaelic-like and do not reflect Greek phonotactics. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since Greek is not Goidelic; check names against those lexicons and avoid collisions.
